internal/terminal: fix go vet %q/uint64 format mismatch in coverage tests

`go vet` flagged 7 Fatalf calls in ansi_coverage_extra_test.go:
%q was given a uint64 (ViewCell.Char) directly instead of a rune,
which vet rejects since %q's meaning differs for numeric vs
string/rune types. Wrapped each with rune(...) — same printed
output, vet-clean. Test logic and assertions unchanged.

Lunobot-Task: fix-vet-ansi-coverage

CI: replace batch gate with a guard against per-ticket bot PRs

ci(quick): never cancel a running check on lunobot/staging

Every bot lands on the same branch, often faster than a run takes, so
cancel-in-progress there would let no run ever finish. Without it GitHub
keeps the running check and replaces only the queued one: each run
completes and the next tests the newest tip, which covers every commit
in between.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix: gosec G115 missed lines + Darwin nice-value raw/true mismatch

Two mechanical gosec misses in plugins/observer (abi.go, runtime.go): a
line identical to an already-//nolint'd one on the line above/below it, just
missing its own comment -- golangci-lint's incremental mode flagged both
once these files became "new" relative to main.

The real bug: plugins/proclist's changePriority (and its test) assumed
x/sys/unix.Getpriority's raw return is always 20-nice. That is true on
Linux (the wrapper calls the raw SYS_GETPRIORITY syscall, bypassing glibc's
own unwrapping), but not on Darwin, where the wrapper calls into libSystem's
getpriority(3) through a dlsym trampoline and already gets the true nice
value back -- confirmed by the failing CI run itself (darwin/arm64:
before=-10 after=19, i.e. exactly the true-nice values Setpriority wrote,
misread as still needing the Linux offset). Split into
priority_raw_linux.go/priority_raw_darwin.go; the test now checks the
outcome (true nice == niceLadder[level]) instead of comparing platform-
dependent raw numbers.

feat(theme): import two Midnight Commander skins as ready styles (f4#239)

Decision (posted in the ticket): a one-off conversion script plus a couple
of ready-made converted themes is enough for a first version -- not a live
in-app mc .ini importer, and not exhaustive [colors]-variable coverage.

- scripts/import_mc_theme.py: converts an mc skin's [core]/[dialog]/[error]
  sections to f4 farcolors entries (internal/theme/colors.go's ColorSlots
  table). Per-filetype highlighting ([filehighlight]) is deliberately not
  converted -- mc's file classes (source, doc, media, ...) are its own
  internal, undocumented extension lists, not something derivable from the
  skin file alone.
- internal/theme/styles/mc_default.ini and mc_dark.ini: real mc skins
  (misc/skins/default.ini and dark.ini from MidnightCommander/mc, not the
  "Solarized"/"Darcula" examples from the original ticket text -- neither
  ships as an actual mc skin, so real ones were used instead), converted
  with the script and layered onto Modern.ini's complete palette so every
  f4 color slot stays defined (required by
  TestBuiltInThemesCoverAllColorSlots) and the groups mc doesn't cover
  (syntax highlighting, the key bar, per-filetype colors, ...) keep a
  sensible look instead of empty gaps.

ProcList: process management, details and configuration (f4#312, parts 3-4 of 4)

Squashed from PR #1592 (migrated to lunobot/staging, LUNOBOT.md § 7.2):
kill (F8), priority (Shift+F1/F2), suspend/resume (Ctrl+F8), process
details dialog (F3), plugin config (F9), plus an inverted-condition fix
in TestSettingsStoreSaveIsAtomic.

Проверить:
1. Открыть список процессов (`Ctrl+Alt+R` или **Команды → Список процессов**) — панель работает так же, как раньше (части 1/2).
2. **F8** на каком-нибудь безопасном процессе (например, запущенном специально для теста) — должен появиться диалог подтверждения с фокусом на Cancel; подтверждение убивает процесс, он пропадает из следующего обновления списка. Отмена — ничего не происходит.
3. **Shift+F1** / **Shift+F2** на процессе — приоритет должен циклически меняться, о каждом изменении (или ошибке, если нет прав) — тост.
4. **Ctrl+F8** на *nix — процесс приостанавливается (перестаёт использовать CPU), повторный `Ctrl+F8` возобновляет; на Windows этой комбинации быть не должно (или явно недоступна).
5. **F3** на процессе — открывается диалог с командной строкой, окружением и списком открытых файлов; на Linux все три раздела заполнены (если хватает прав), на Windows/macOS — только путь к исполняемому файлу, без падений на процессах с недоступным окружением.
6. **F9 → «Конфигурация плагина» → ProcList** — снять галочку у одного из столбцов, изменить интервал обновления, сохранить. Открыть панель заново — должен измениться набор столбцов и скорость обновления. Попытка снять галочки со всех столбцов — сохранение должно быть отклонено (валидация `Settings.validate`).

Merge branch 'main' of https://github.com/unxed/f4

panel: isolate the drive-menu Ctrl+N tests' FrameManager

TestDriveMenu_CtrlNOpensBookmarkEditor and
TestDriveMenu_CtrlNThroughFrameManagerDoesNotForkWorkspace were the only
two Ctrl+N tests in menukeys_test.go that called vtui.FrameManager.Init
directly instead of testutil.SwapFrameManager, even though both call
ResizeConsole, which starts two real directory-load workers (the panels
default to "."). Init resets the frame stack but, deliberately, not the
manager's task queue, so a background worker left running past an
earlier test -- its own from a previous run, or another test's -- can
still post to this same process-wide vtui.FrameManager singleton while
these two tests are asserting against it. That is exactly the class of
leak e58d6bd7 fixed for FileSystemPanel's own load queue a few commits
back, just against the frame stack this time instead of a WaitGroup:
CI saw TestDriveMenu_CtrlNThroughFrameManagerDoesNotForkWorkspace fail
once on a linux/arm64 shuffle run (PR #1587) with an extra frame having
landed on the stack right as the test's Ctrl+N reached
vtui.FrameManager's real dispatcher, tripping its own screen-count
check; the same shuffle seed did not reproduce it on a second run,
consistent with a timing race rather than a fixed order dependency, and
main's own most recent run passed this test cleanly.

Both tests now use the package's swapFrameManager helper, which joins
every process-wide directory-load worker before installing a fresh
FrameManager instance that no other test's goroutine ever held a
reference to -- the same isolation their sibling tests in this file
(TestBookmarksDialog_/TestAssociationsEditor_*ThroughFrameManager*)
already use.
